newsitem.title: GERMANY: Dresdner-Frankfurt still investment banking site.
newsitem.headline: Dresdner-Frankfurt still investment banking site.

text.p: Dresdner Bank AG, highlighting again a sharp strategic contrast with rival Deutsche Bank AG, on Thursday stressed that control of its investment banking business would continue to be split between Frankfurt and London.
"I wish to stress firmly once again: We do not want to concentrate investment banking in one financial centre," chairman Juergen Sarrazin told a news conference.

Dresdner would instead build up its strengths in different financial centres and "manage the various business areas from whichever site (that would yield)...the best competitive advantage," Sarrazin said.

The firm message follows Dresdner's parting last month with Dresdner Kleinwort Benson chairman Simon Robertson, whom the bank accused of a "narrow" approach in seeking to centralise management power in London.
Robertson's views were irreconcilable with its own, Dresdner said.

Under its latest organisational plan, Dresdner has decided to centralise management of its corporate finance and equities operations in London, but wants Frankfurt to retain primary responsibility for its fixed income business.
Frankfurt and London will share management of the Global Finance activities, which cover syndicated loans and project financing, Sarrazin said.

All these activities will carry the Dresdner Kleinwort Benson brand, adopted after Dresdner took over Kleinwort in 1995, and will be co-ordinated by a management council of Frankfurt and London managers and regional directors.
Dresdner committed itself from the start to splitting responsibility for investment banking between Britain and Germany.

Its attitude marked a stark contrast to Deutsche Bank AG, which outraged lobbyists for Frankfurt as a financial centre when it picked the London-based Deutsche Morgan Grenfell as the hub of its investment banking activities.
Detailing Dresdner's performance in 1996 on Thursday, Sarrazin said that worldwide investment banking activities contributed a three-digit million mark sum to earnings.
But he declined to comment specifically on how Kleinwort performed during the year, which was the first in which Kleinwort was consolidated for all four quarters.
Dresdner itself posted a 30.7 percent rise in net income in 1996 to 1.58 billion marks and a 44 percent rise in operating profit to 2.86 billion.
Deutsche's 1996 results showed its experience with British-based investment banking had not been entirely problem-free.

The bank suffered major embarrassments in its fund management arm in the last year, with charges arising from a fund mismanagement scandal at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell estimated at more than one billion marks.
The charge comprises compensation and fines after fund manager Peter Young was found to have overvalued investments under his control.
Deutsche reported a 4.5 percent rise in net income to 2.2 billion marks in 1996, and a 37 percent increase in operating profit to 5.8 billion marks.
